{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q018_tal_effector_repeat_lengths","answer":"They share a homologous repeat architecture; SCOPe family membership does not require equal sequence length or equal numbers of repeats. In SCOPe 2.08, the returned domain SEQRES sequences are 51 residues for d2kq5a_ (PthA), 373 for d3v6pa_ (dHax3), and 752 for d4cj9a_ (BurrH). These are classified structural constructs, not necessarily full-length native proteins.

TAL-family proteins contain tandem, short, predominantly α-helical repeats. Canonical TAL repeats are approximately 34 residues long, with two helices connected by a variable loop. Repeating the same structural building block produces an extended superhelical array. Thus, the short PthA fragment samples only a small part of the repeat architecture, whereas dHax3 and BurrH contain much longer arrays. Repeat number, construct boundaries, and terminal segments can change total length greatly without changing family identity. BurrH also illustrates that the family accommodates divergent TAL-like repeat sequences.

The release-specific hierarchy is family a.298.1.1, TAL (transcription activator-like) effector (sunid 267609); superfamily a.298.1, TAL effector-like; fold a.298, Left-handed alpha-alpha superhelix; and class a, all-alpha proteins. Family membership supports a shared evolutionary relationship, rather than merely a similar helical appearance. Superfamily membership supports broader common ancestry; fold or class membership alone would not establish homology.

This classification does not establish identical DNA targets, biological roles, or transcription-activation activity for all three constructs. Specificity depends on the repeat recognition residues and their order and requires sequence and functional evidence. Likewise, the 51-residue fragment can inform local repeat structure but cannot by itself represent the curvature, repeat register, or DNA contacts of a complete array; template selection must account for repeat count and construct coverage.","evidence_used":["Pretrained model knowledge","/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d2kq5a_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d3v6pa_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d4cj9a_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/a.298.1.1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/264989","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/265556","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/265996","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267647","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d2kq5a_?release=2.08","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d3v6pa_?release=2.08","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d4cj9a_?release=2.08","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267609","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267704","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267705","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267596","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267589"]}]}
